info.name: TradeMaster IMS Backend — Complete REST API
info.description:
Source-derived Postman Collection v2.1 for the existing TradeMaster Spring Boot backend. Covers all 45 REST controllers: 286 distinct HTTP method/path pairs represented by 294 requests, including eight separate multipart variants of JSON operations.

Set username and password locally, send Authentication / Login, then inherit Bearer {{jwt}}. The four forgot-password operations and public profile-file download use No Auth. Credentials and JWT defaults are intentionally empty.

The baseUrl includes /api and has no trailing slash. Every path-variable numeric 0 and JSON foreign-key ID 0 is a placeholder requiring an existing test record. Example codes/names are placeholders; repeated creates may violate unique constraints. Required and defaulted query parameters are enabled; optional filters without defaults are disabled. Dates are sample ISO values, not live data.

Multipart JSON model parts are actual MultipartFile uploads: choose a local JSON file using each part description as its content example. Select actual image/attachment/CSV files manually. No companion files or absolute local upload paths are created.

Many requests create, modify, approve, cancel, delete, send email or change passwords. Review and send selected requests only against an authorized test target. This collection does not auto-run or chain destructive operations. All examples and status expectations come from controller/model/service source, not production responses.

Controller-declared mappings are documented; implicit framework HEAD/OPTIONS handling and static /uploads/** resource handlers are not additional API requests. Response examples are intentionally empty because no production API responses were captured.

request.description:
POST /api/auth/login

Source: src/main/java/com/trademaster/ims/controller/AuthController.java:54 (authenticateUser).

Authentication: public; no Bearer token required.

Content type: application/json.

This operation can modify application data or trigger external work. Review the payload and use an authorized test target before sending.

JSON is a source-derived example, not a populated production record. Replace every numeric ID 0 and example identifier before sending.

Set collection username and password locally. A successful response returns token; the test script stores it in collection variable jwt. A failed login clears jwt. The login updates last-login and audit records.

Status tests assert the successful controller contract with valid inputs, existing records and sufficient permissions; placeholder requests are not proof of a successful live API call.

exec: pm.collectionVariables.unset('jwt');
pm.test('Login succeeds with valid configured credentials', function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });
if (pm.response.code === 200) {
var data = pm.response.json();
pm.test('Response contains a nonempty JWT token', function () { pm.expect(data.token).to.be.a('string').and.not.empty; });
if (typeof data.token === 'string' && data.token.length > 0) { pm.collectionVariables.set('jwt', data.token); }
else { pm.collectionVariables.unset('jwt'); }
} else { pm.collectionVariables.unset('jwt'); }
